receipt_statuses.label: Pending Submission
receipt_statuses.meaning: The filing was created but has not been successfully submitted yet.

receipt_statuses.label: Submitted
receipt_statuses.meaning: The filing was successfully submitted but had not yet been reviewed by the court.

receipt_statuses.label: Filed
receipt_statuses.meaning: All documents and requests in the submission were accepted/filed by the court.

receipt_statuses.label: Partially Filed
receipt_statuses.meaning: Some documents or requests were accepted/filed and some were not filed.

receipt_statuses.label: Not Filed
receipt_statuses.meaning: All documents and requests in the submission were not filed.

jurisdictions.name: Oklahoma County, Oklahoma
jurisdictions.status_label: Official sources located; live route not tested
jurisdictions.route_scope: Published Oklahoma District Courts civil e-filing materials; Oklahoma County is listed in the January 2025 county FAQ. Current county-by-case-type availability was not tested.
jurisdictions.summary: The Version 2 guide documents new civil case filing and document attachments. The current registration page says pro se filing is not supported. These materials do not establish what a separate child-welfare intake form accepts or how that form routes evidence.

access: The current OUCMS registration page states that pro se filings are not supported.
The Oklahoma County Court Clerk page says its e-file system is available for attorneys and state agencies. The Version 2 guide also describes process-server use.
The FAQ dated January 28, 2025 says conventional paper filing remained available at that time. The current alternative path for self-represented people has not been independently confirmed.
document_inputs: The Version 2 guide calls for text-based PDFs. If the original cannot be converted, it says a non-text-searchable PDF may be submitted; it also allows a non-text image in the current JPEG standard.
Attachments and exhibits are associated with a principal filing; each document is submitted as a separate file, and the documents must be associated with the same case.
The guide states that confidential or sealed documents could not be filed through e-filing at the time of that version. Current handling needs confirmation.
receipt: Pending Submission means the filing was created but not successfully submitted.
Submitted means it was successfully submitted but had not yet been reviewed by the court.
Filed, Partially Filed, and Not Filed are later clerk-processing outcomes defined by the guide.
For a new civil case, the guide says the first confirmation uses a temporary reference; an official case number follows clerk acceptance.

jurisdictions.scope_note: The January 2025 FAQ says new-case e-filing was not yet available. The newer Version 2 guide, dated October 14, 2025, includes new civil-case filing. The map records this source timeline; it does not assume current availability for every county, case type, or filer. The child-welfare intake form remains a separate, unidentified process.
